text:
Noel Acciari signed with Philadelphia on July 1 to bring a hard edge to the bottom of the lineup, and on Saturday against Columbus he did the kind of thing that justifies it. PHLY Sports' Charlie O'Connor, who admitted he "didn't like how much Acciari was playing in the 3rd period", still called it "one hell of a play by him to bat down that clear" before Denver Barkey's go-ahead goal. That came three days after RotoWire reported he was hurt against Edmonton, where he played 6.4 minutes; he was back for 16.5 against Columbus.

He has 3 goals and 5 points in 22 games, roughly what his chances deserve, plus 48 hits. The concern is five on five, where the Flyers have had only 41.6% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, 2 points worse than without him. That's hard to square with last season, when Evolving-Hockey had him in the 98th percentile among forwards at taking chances away, against competition in the 93rd percentile. At 34, undrafted out of Providence and on his sixth NHL team, he's paid to make that number better.
headline: Acciari is doing exactly what Philadelphia signed him for
